criteria_source: The fixture only. db.js's write() is the single helper every route mutation calls, and its own comment says it exists so there is exactly one place a transaction begins; auth.js sets req.user on every request. Written from those files, not from rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the audit capture sits at the one point every write already flows through - db.js's write() helper (with the acting user threaded to it), or the database itself via triggers with the actor set on the transaction - so a route handler added next month is audited without anyone remembering to. Fails when it proposes adding an audit call inside each route handler separately, which silently misses the next handler someone writes, or a standalone audit service consuming events the handlers would each have to emit, or when it never identifies that a single write path exists.
